title: REPORT on the implementation of the common foreign and security policy – annual report 2025
part_text: 22. Underlines that sustainable peace requires a credible political process aimed at achieving a two-state solution based on the 1967 lines, with two sovereign, democratic states as peaceful neighbours and with Jerusalem as a shared capital; calls on all parties to renew efforts to remove the obstacles to this solution and condemns the expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank and East Jerusalem as such an obstacle; welcomes sanctions adopted against extremist Israeli settlers; underscores the role of the Palestinian Authority as the EU’s main interlocutor in Palestine and reaffirms that any future governance in Gaza must exclude the participation of terrorist organisations and must ensure the demilitarisation of Gaza; reiterates its opposition to any annexation plan for Gaza or any other Palestinian territory and against mass forcible transfers; strongly condemns Palestinian terrorism and support for it, and underlines that terrorism runs counter to a peaceful resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict;
